ca_don_t_call_me_dome.blurb: A small, quiet dome in the Glen Aulin corner of Tuolumne Meadows, reached on foot from the Twin Bridges crossing of the Tuolumne River. The 18 routes mix short bolted lines with a few crack climbs, on granodiorite that is described as excellent. Difficulty is concentrated in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with a couple of 5.12s, one 5.13 and a handful of easier pitches in the 5.7 to 5.9 range. Plenty of sun reaches the faces, and crowds are light compared with the roadside Tuolumne domes. A single rope and a rack of quickdraws cover most of what is here, which makes it a good half-day objective for a party wanting solitude.

ca_west_face_16.blurb: The main climbing face of East Cottage Dome (also called Erratic Dome) in Tuolumne Meadows, holding most of the dome's routes. Eighteen climbs here are steep knob-and-face lines, mostly bolted or mixed, all falling in the 5.10 to 5.11 band with roughly equal numbers at each. The style rewards steady footwork on small knobs and holds rather than cracks. The dome sits at around 8,800 feet, so it suits summer and early fall. The walk from the road reaches the base by working left past a black wall and then a short class 2-3 scramble up to the climbs.

ca_f_liberty_cap.blurb: A big granite dome above Yosemite Valley, sitting beside Nevada Fall and the John Muir Trail. The wall is a serious multi-pitch objective, with routes running from roughly nine to fifteen pitches up splitter cracks and large corners. Most of the 18 listed lines are aid climbs, alongside a few trad lines; the free grades cluster from 5.8 up to 5.12, with several at the top end. The southwest face is the dominant wall. Expect a long approach on the Mist Trail, a loose ledge system to reach the base, and a committing day. The summit gives wide views over Little Yosemite Valley and Half Dome.

ca_roadwork_wall.blurb: A cliff above the Whitney Portal road in the eastern Sierra, just right of the Solstice Celebration wall. It is mainly a trad venue, with two sport lines among its 18 routes, and the climbing is predominantly in the 5.10 range, with a handful of 5.9s and just a few easier or harder outliers. Routes tend toward sustained edges and smears on generally good rock, with a few flaky spots that should clean up with traffic. Some lines start from a ledge in the middle of the wall that takes fourth-class climbing to reach. The descent is a third-class walk off to the left.

ca_upper_willow_creek_wall_area.blurb: A small satellite wall in the Fresno Dome (Wamello) area off Highway 41, perched a short uphill walk above the lower Willow Creek Wall. Eighteen routes, mostly bolted sport lines with a few trad lines and one top-rope, run from 5.8 to 5.11 with an even split between 5.10 and 5.11 and a good number of moderates. It makes a handy add-on or warm-up near the dome's longer trad routes. The area sits around 6,500 feet, so the granite is comfortable for climbing in the cooler parts of summer and into fall.

ca_tiger_cage.blurb: A small crag tucked off the road near Courtright Reservoir in the southern Sierra, at about 5,000 feet. The 18 routes are mostly trad cracks, with a couple of top-rope lines, running from easy fifth class up to 5.11. Most of the grades fall between 5.9 and 5.10, with a few at 5.8 and below. You will find steep cracks, thin friction slab and some steeper face climbing. Anchors at the top let you top-rope many of the lines. The trail in is faint, so allow extra time on a first visit to locate the base.
